annotation.title_clean: Part 255—Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising
annotation.title_en: Part 255—Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising
annotation.venue: Code of Federal Regulations (16 CFR Part 255)
annotation.summary_en: The FTC's revised Guides (16 CFR Part 255, 2023) explain how Section 5 of the FTC Act applies to endorsements and testimonials in advertising. They cover consumer and expert endorsements, fake reviews, disclosure of material connections, and clear and conspicuous disclosure. They are not about AI or robotics; a robot forum example is incidental.
key_provisions_or_claims: Endorsements must reflect honest opinions and experience of the endorser, and endorsers must be bona fide users where claimed.
Unexpected material connections between endorsers and advertisers must be clearly and conspicuously disclosed.
Advertisers, endorsers and intermediaries can be liable for deceptive endorsements; advertisers should guide and monitor endorsers.
Advertisers must not suppress, distort or fake consumer reviews, and fake reviews are deceptive.
Typicality claims in testimonials require substantiation or disclosure of generally expected results.
